reference/ac-classes.md.content:
# Acceptance criteria and Integration

An acceptance criterion states a functionality or a constraint the change delivers: what is observed, not how it is built. One row may cover several scenarios of one functionality. It holds when the files at the delivered commit make it true and a check run in a checkout of that commit shows it.

Everything else asked around the change is an `Integration` entry. An entry is one list item in its source's words, never judged and never blocking.

## Entry kinds

| Kind | Example |
|---|---|
| `person step` | the operator runs the cutover |

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Only placement moved. After writes the Integration entry as a list item in the ticket's exact words, with a separate marker line (`ticket row, not an acceptance criterion: person step`). Before folds a bare kind label into the item (`- person step: the operator starts the cutover`), so the item is not purely the source's words and nothing marks it as a ticket row. I read that as failing the 'ticket marker' clause, though it is a close call: Before does move the text verbatim and labels it a person step, so a looser reading would pass it. Ownership did not move as you expected: Before already renumbered both legs correctly (orchard/importer to `scope: AC 1`, orchard/reports to `scope: AC 2`), so it holds on both sides and the scope-rewrite wording shows no gain on this sample. No-question holds in both: neither spec nor audit asks anything, and both audits apply the chair's cluster with its grounding citation. To keep all three, keep the instruction that the moved row stays an unprefixed verbatim list item with the ticket/person-step marker on its own line, and keep the same-edit rule that every leg's scope is renumbered to its original functionality rows. One difference to check against the unchanged audit contract: After drops the per-line `Applied:` prefix that Before used inside the Applied section, so state the audit line format explicitly if that prefix is required.

The two functionality rows remain verbatim and in order in both outputs. Ownership held in both: Before already renumbered orchard/importer to `scope: AC 1` and orchard/reports to `scope: AC 2`, so the expected fails -> holds movement for ownership did not show on this sample; the scope-rewrite wording is not what changed the result here, though it is harmless and the audit now states the renumbering explicitly. No-question held in both: neither spec nor audit asks a placement or ownership question, and the audit applies the chair's cluster with Deferred and Rejected as none. To keep all three, retain the wording that requires the marker on the moved entry itself in the spec (not only in the audit), keep the instruction to rewrite every leg's scope in the same edit, and keep the 'without a question' phrasing; consider fixing the exact marker text so the entry stays one list item in the source's words with a consistent annotation.
